I have the complete answer from the documents.

## Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby

Per **SOP-02** and **EQ-01**, a reflow oven in standby still draws **36% of its 70 kW rating = 25.2 kW** for as long as it stays on — a large, continuous load that produces nothing. A properly switched-off oven uses only about 340–350 kWh per oven-weekend (just residual heat-up). So leaving an oven in standby all weekend wastes far more than a full normal weekend's energy from a single oven. The rule is: switch ovens **off, not to standby**, for weekends and holidays, and only after the 30-minute post-line warm period and when no boards are inside.

## Excess energy in incident S5

During incident S5 (2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20), RF-02 was left in standby all weekend:

- Weekend energy: **~1,556 kWh** vs. **~346 kWh** normal
- **Excess: ~1,210 kWh** from that single oven

Note that the off-schedule rule only flags this after 120 minutes above 20% of rating, so the real benefit comes from preventing it (switching off) rather than detecting it afterward.

I have the complete answer from both the load-shed playbook and the never-shed list.

## Load shedding order (SOP-03 / EM-02)

Per the load-shed playbook, actions are applied in order of least disruption first [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]:

| Order | Action | Equipment |
|---|---|---|
| **1 — shed first** | Pause EV charging | EV-01 |
| 2 | Delay next burn-in loading | BI-01, BI-02 |
| 3 | Raise chilled-water setpoint +1 °C | CH-01, CH-02 |
| 4 | Lower compressed-air pressure 0.5 bar | AC-01, AC-02, AC-03 |

**EV charging (EV-01) is shed first** because it has no effect on production [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook].

## Loads that must never be shed

The following are never shed under any condition [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook > Never shed]:

- **Server room (DC-01)** — a continuous critical load [source: docs/knowledge/equipment/EQ-12_server_room.md#EQ-12 Server Room Manual > Purpose and scope]
- **Running molders mid-cycle (IM-01 to IM-04)**
- **Reflow ovens with boards inside (RF-01 to RF-03)**

These are confirmed in both the EM-02 playbook and SOP-06 heat-wave pre-cooling guidance [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-06_heat_wave_precooling.md#SOP-06 Heat Wave Pre-cooling > Never shed].
